title: Jesus Christ Is Risen Today

text.name: Lyra Davidica
text.role: Anonymous English translation (1708); verses 2 and 3 from John Arnold's Compleat Psalmodist (1749)

description: Jesus Christ Is Risen Today in Tonic Solfa to EASTER HYMN, doh is C: the solfa with the words and alleluias, staff notation, four verses and a piano.
about: The first verse is an anonymous translation of a medieval Latin Easter carol, printed with this tune in Lyra Davidica (London, 1708). Later verses came from John Arnold's Compleat Psalmodist (1749) and Charles Wesley (1740).
Every line ends with a long Alleluia: the first syllable is sung over five quick notes, so it is worth practising the Alleluia on its own before the verses.
underlay: Je-sus Christ is ris’n to-day,_ Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Our tri-um-phant ho-ly day,_ Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Who did once up-on the cross Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Suf_-fer_ to re-deem our loss._ Al_____-le_-lu_-ia!

lines: Jesus Christ is risen today, Alleluia!
Who did once upon the cross, Alleluia!
Suffer to redeem our loss. Alleluia!
Hymns of praise then let us sing, Alleluia!
Unto Christ, our heavenly King, Alleluia!
Who endured the cross and grave, Alleluia!
Sinners to redeem and save. Alleluia!
But the pains which He endured, Alleluia!
Now above the sky He’s King, Alleluia!
Where the angels ever sing. Alleluia!
Sing we to our God above, Alleluia!
Praise eternal as His love; Alleluia!
Praise Him, all ye heavenly host, Alleluia!
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Alleluia!
